subject: ash-buried town volcano
title: What If a Capital City Was Abandoned? Montserrat's Still Is, Officially

scenes.text: What if a capital city had to be abandoned? One was in 1997. Officially, it's still the capital.
Plymouth, on the Caribbean island of Montserrat. Four thousand people, the shops, the port, the government. All beside a volcano.
In July 1995 the Soufriere Hills volcano began erupting, and the town was evacuated.
June 25th, 1997: surges of hot gas and ash raced downhill and killed 19 people who had stayed in the zone.
That August, ash buried 80 percent of the town. In places it would pile 15 metres deep. The island's whole southern half was closed.
Two thirds of the islanders left for good. Government moved north. But no law ever replaced Plymouth, so it's the only ghost town that's still a capital.

description:
What if a capital city had to be abandoned? Plymouth, capital of the Caribbean island of Montserrat, was evacuated when the Soufriere Hills volcano reawakened in 1995 and abandoned for good in 1997, after pyroclastic surges killed 19 people and ash buried about 80 percent of the town.
Two thirds of the island's population emigrated, the southern half of Montserrat is an exclusion zone, and government moved to Brades, yet Plymouth remains the de jure capital, the only ghost town that is officially a capital.
What should we run through next?

first_comment: Montserrat had about 15,000 people before the eruption; today just over 5,000 live in the northern safe zone, and a new capital is being built at Little Bay. Which disaster what-if should we run through next?
